cell_type_context: Mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells; FGF2 stimulation with STAT5 activation, PLF1/PLF4 expression and endothelial morphogenesis assays
compartment_context: Extracellular FGF2; plasma-membrane FGF receptor; receptor-proximal SH2B1/SH2-Bbeta; nuclear STAT5 and PLF1 regulatory region
injury_context: no SCI transfer inferred; endothelial angiogenesis comparator model only
context_scope: Primary studies support FGF2-dependent STAT5 activation and PLF1/proliferin induction, including STAT5 occupancy at the PLF1 promoter. The output studies do not resolve FGFR3 as the receptor subtype, so the existing FGFR3-SH2B1-STAT5 backbone is retained as a composite, receptor-subtype-bounded evidence route.
assay_or_perturbation: FGF2 stimulation; phospho-STAT5 and STAT5 DNA-binding assays; dominant-negative or constitutively active STAT5; PLF1/PLF4 RNA or protein measurements; STAT5 ChIP at PLF1 promoter; endothelial migration, invasion and tube-formation assays
citation_note: Primary studies report FGF2-dependent STAT5 activation and STAT5-dependent PLF1/proliferin induction with PLF1 promoter occupancy; primary locators: PMID:19176400 and PMID:22199350
evidence_summary: Primary-supported claim: FGF2 activates STAT5 in mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells and induces PLF1/proliferin expression; STAT5 perturbation reduces the output and STAT5 occupancy is detected at the PLF1 promoter. This supplies a target-gene output for the existing FGF2-FGFR3-SH2B1-STAT5 evidence backbone while preserving receptor-subtype uncertainty.
limitations: The output studies establish FGF2-to-STAT5-to-PLF1 evidence in endothelial cells but do not identify FGFR3 as the relevant FGF receptor subtype or establish a single linear SH2B1 relay in the same assay. No SCI transfer, causal graph traversal or database confidence score is asserted.
